candidate_sentences.text: Annualised like-for-like rental income growth was 4.9 percent, compared to 5.6 percent in the previous year, driven primarily by indexation.
Real economic occupancy remained steady at 98.5 percent.
Consequently, net operating income improved to SEK 11,475 million from SEK 11,188 million, pushing the last-twelve-months net operating income margin up to 72.1 percent from 70.3 percent.

Fair value changes of investment properties yielded a positive increase of 2.9 percent, or SEK 9,498 million, bringing total investment property fair value to SEK 324,429 million compared to SEK 335,422 million at the end of 2024.
The company actively pursued its privatisation strategy, generating SEK 10,664 million through the sale of 2,466 residential units at a 28.9 percent premium to book value.
Net loan-to-value improved to 52.2 percent from 56.4 percent, and the interest coverage ratio strengthened to 2.0x from 1.9x.

verified_key_information_units.information: Q4 2025 performance: like-for-like rental growth of 4.6% (5.3% in Q4 2024), rental income decreased 3.4% to SEK 3,945 million, real economic occupancy rose to 98.7% (98.6% in Q4 2024), net operating income margin held at 70.2% (LTM margin 72.1%), privatization sales of SEK 2,890 million (798 units at 32.5% premium vs 24% in Q4 2024), property values up 0.5%, goodwill impairment loss of SEK 3,707 million, and credit metrics at Net LTV 52.2% (56.4%) and ICR 2.0x (1.9x).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Q4 Highlights, Key Figures table for Q4

verified_key_information_units.information: Operational performance drivers: standing assets contributed SEK 800 million rental income growth via indexation, tenant improvements, and occupancy gains; like-for-like growth decomposed into indexations (3.3% of 4.9% annual growth), tenant improvements (0.7%), occupancy improvements (0.7%), and rent reversion (0.2%); property expenses decreased 6.1% annually to SEK 4,378 million due to digitalisation and portfolio contraction; capital expenditures of SEK 3,893 million allocated to maintenance (SEK 1,790m), sustainability (SEK 557m), tenant improvements (SEK 1,168m), and value-add (SEK 241m).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Rental Income Development, Like-for-like Development, Property Expenses, Asset Management sections

verified_key_information_units.information: Country-specific investment property fair value developments: Sweden +0.8% (SEK 717m) from rental performance; Germany +1.2% (SEK 926m) despite privatisation strategy shift; Denmark +7.2% (SEK 4,643m) from ownership market strength; Czechia +6.7% (SEK 1,856m) from rental growth; Netherlands +5.4% (SEK 1,424m) with privatisation as highest-and-best use; Norway -2.7% (SEK -382m) from buy-to-let supply increase; UK -0.4% (SEK -20m) from yield stabilisation; Poland +4.1% (SEK 173m) and Finland +4.3% (SEK 161m) from rental growth and rent reversion.

verified_key_information_units.information: Liquidity and financing: Heimstaden Bostad completed SEK 59,500 million financing (refinancings and new financings); liability management in January 2025 issued SEK 750 million senior unsecured floating rate notes and EUR 430 million/400 million fixed rate notes while tendering existing maturities; interest expenses of SEK 6,536 million (average rate 3.43% vs 3.01% in 2024); interest coverage ratio improved to 2.0x (1.9x); net loan-to-value decreased to 52.2% (56.4%); unutilised credit facilities of SEK 23,449 million at parent level.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Funding section, Interest Expenses, Liability Management, Alternative Performance Measures

Heimstaden also executed liability management exercises, issuing SEK 750 million and EUR 830 million in senior unsecured notes to tender near-term maturities.

verified_key_information_units.information: Sustainability performance: weather-corrected energy intensity reduced 10% to 148 kWh/m² (exceeding 2% target); GHG emissions reduced 14.2% against 2020 baseline (on track for 42% reduction by 2030); EU Taxonomy-aligned revenue at 22% (26% in 2024) and capex at 18% (22% in 2024); green assets valued at approximately SEK 76 billion supported green bond issuance of SEK 13,767 million in FY25; sustainability-linked loans of SEK 5,818 million all met KPIs (Sustainalytics Negligible Risk, SBTi emission target achievement).

details.completeness_justification: K3, K5 and K6 are fully covered. K1 and K2 are only partially covered (missing several core components such as Q4-specific rental income, occupancy, NOI margin, property value change, privatisation sales and credit metrics). K4 and K7 are entirely absent.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. Each sentence follows logically from the preceding statements: operational metrics (S2–S6) lead directly to the NOI margin improvement, which in turn supports the profit-before-tax and net-profit figures (S8). Valuation changes (S7) are presented as an independent driver of the profit increase. The privatisation proceeds (S9) are explicitly linked to debt reduction and the resulting credit-metric improvements (S10–S11). Financing activities (S12–S14) are presented as separate but complementary actions that reinforce the balance-sheet strengthening narrative. No sentence contradicts another, and the overall structure moves from operations to valuation, profitability, capital allocation, and financing without repetition or organisational gaps.
